title: Measuring spectral reflectance and transmittance of small and narrow leaves
author: Etienne Laliberté
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q56dy9e
materials: Spectra Vista Corporation DC-R/T Integrating Sphere

steps.title: Prepare Sample Mounts and Platforms
steps.instruction: Construct the necessary hardware to hold the leaf samples.

substeps.instruction: Build at least six sample mounts from thin plastic (e.g., acetate sheets) with a square window larger than the sample port lip (e.g., 2.5 cm x 2.5 cm).
Build at least six sample platforms from thin cardboard (e.g., file folders) to create a flat surface when attached to the integrating sphere.

steps.title: Assemble Leaf Arrays
steps.instruction: Fix leaves onto the sample mounts to create six distinct leaf arrays (#1-6).

substeps.instruction: Tape leaves onto the sample mount, positioning as much material as possible in the center of the port.
Separate leaves by approximately 1 mm to avoid multiple scattering.
If leaves are shorter than 1.25 cm, fix them by their petiole with tape in one or two rows.
Sandwich the sample mount holding each leaf array between the two sides of a cardboard sample platform and fix with tape.

steps.title: Initialize Spectroradiometer and Software
steps.instruction: Set up the instrument and data management system.

substeps.instruction: Power on the spectroradiometer and warm up for >15 min.
Power on the integrating sphere lamp and warm up for >5 min.
Connect the spectroradiometer to the computer via Bluetooth (default password: hr1024i).
In the software, select File > Data Options > Auto Save.
Create a new working folder in the shared 'spectra' Google Drive CABO folder named YYYYstarted-YourLastName-Degree-University.
Create a subfolder named YYYY-MM-DD-SiteID-SpectroradiometerSerialNumber and keep the default file base name (grMMDDYY).
Connect the instrument via Control > Setup Instrument.
Configure settings: Choose RAW DN optic, 5 sec scan time, Auto Integration, and verify date/time and Integration Scales Raw DN Data.
In Control > Overlap / Matching Settings: Select 'Preserve Overlapped Detector Data' and set Matching Type to 'None'.

steps.title: Hardware Installation and Alignment
steps.instruction: Install the sphere and verify light path alignment.

substeps.instruction: Install the integrating sphere onto the spectroradiometer (refer to SVC manual p. 6-16).
Screw the tethered light trap onto the reflectance port sample holder (can remain for the session).
Screw the tethered light trap onto the transmission port sample holder.
Check lamp alignment: Place a thin piece of paper at the reflectance sample port exit to ensure the beam under-fills and is centered (refer to SVC manual p. 29-32 if adjustment is needed).

steps.title: Reflectance Mode Calibration
steps.instruction: Collect reference and stray light scans for reflectance measurements.

substeps.instruction: Place the tethered calibrated Spectralon® reflectance standard over the reflectance port so the beam shines directly on the reflective surface; collect a 'Target Scan' (R ref,p).
Remove the filter paper from the transmission port sample holder.
Remove the Spectralon® standard from the reflectance port.
Place the Spectralon® standard over the transmission port; collect a 'Target Scan' (R str).
Remove the Spectralon® standard from the sphere reflectance port.
Remove the light trap from the transmission port sample holder.

steps.title: Transmittance Mode Reference Scan
steps.instruction: Establish the reference radiance for transmittance measurements.

substeps.instruction: Position the lamp over the sphere primary light entrance port and secure it in the locked position (use slotted heat shield).
Install the Spectralon® plug over the primary light port, ensuring the curved plug matches the sphere's curvature.
Collect a 'Reference Scan' (T ref).
Gently pull the lamp and transmission port sample holder away from the sphere.

steps.title: Transmittance Measurements (Arrays 1-3)
steps.instruction: Measure target radiance for the first three leaf arrays in transmittance mode.

substeps.instruction: Place sample platform with leaf array #1 over the transmission port, abaxial (lower) surfaces facing into the sphere.
Lock the lamp back into position.
Replace leaf array #1 with #2, then #2 with #3.
Collect a 'Target Scan' for leaf array #3 (T tar,3).
Remove leaf array #6 from the transmission sample port holder (as specified in text).

steps.title: Reflectance Measurements (Arrays 1-3)
steps.instruction: Measure adaxial reflectance and gap fraction for the first three arrays.

substeps.instruction: Remove the sample platform holding leaf array #1 from the transmission port.
Position leaf array #1 over the transmission port, adaxial (upper) surfaces facing into the sphere; collect a 'Target Scan'.
Place filter paper directly behind sample platform #1; collect a 'Target Scan' (R tar,p) by placing the paper over the reflectance port.
Position sample platform #1 in front of the filter paper over the reflectance port (adaxial surfaces facing in); collect a 'Target Scan' (R tar,ap,1).
Repeat the process for leaf array #2: collect R tar,ap,2 (with paper) and R tar,a,2 (without paper).
Repeat the process for leaf array #3: collect R tar,ap,3 (with paper) and R tar,a,3 (without paper).
Collect a 'Target Scan' for leaf array #1 in reflectance mode (R tar,a,1).

steps.title: Transmittance Measurements (Arrays 1-2)
steps.instruction: Collect target radiance for arrays 1 and 2 in transmittance mode.

substeps.instruction: Remove leaf array #3 from the reflectance port.
Remove leaf array #1 and filter paper from the transmission port.
Place the Spectralon® standard over the transmission port.
Position sample platform #1 over the reflectance port, abaxial surfaces facing in; collect a 'Target Scan'.
Remove leaf array #1 from the reflectance port.
Collect a 'Target Scan' for leaf array #1 (T tar,1) and leaf array #2 (T tar,2).
Position sample platform #1 over the reflectance port (abaxial surfaces facing in) and collect a second 'Target Scan' for stability assessment.

steps.title: Reflectance Measurements (Arrays 4-6)
steps.instruction: Measure adaxial reflectance and gap fraction for the remaining arrays.

substeps.instruction: Assemble leaf arrays #4, #5, and #6 onto sample mounts and platforms as described in Step 2.
Place filter paper behind sample platform #1; collect 'Target Scans' for R ref,ap (for arrays 4-6) and R ref,ap (for arrays 1-3).
Remove Spectralon® standard from the transmission port.
Collect a 'Target Scan' for R ref,ap (arrays 4-6).
Collect a 'Reference Scan' for R ref,a (arrays 1-3).
Remove Spectralon® standard from the reflectance port.
Remove leaf array #1 and filter paper from the transmission port.
Place Spectralon® standard over the transmission port.
For leaf array #4: Position over reflectance port with filter paper (adaxial facing in) to collect R tar,ap,4; then remove paper to collect R tar,a,4.
For leaf array #5: Position over reflectance port with filter paper (adaxial facing in) to collect R tar,ap,5; then remove paper to collect R tar,a,5.
For leaf array #6: Position over reflectance port with filter paper (adaxial facing in) to collect R tar,ap,6; then remove paper to collect R tar,a,6.

steps.title: Final Stability and Transmittance Scans
steps.instruction: Perform final system checks and complete transmittance measurements for arrays 4-6.

substeps.instruction: Remove leaf array #6 from the reflectance port.
Remove Spectralon® standard from the transmission port.
Place Spectralon® standard over the reflectance port.
Position leaf array #1 over the transmission port (adaxial facing in); collect a 'Target Scan' for stability.
Place filter paper behind sample platform #1; collect a 'Target Scan' for stability.
Replace leaf array #3 with #4; collect 'Target Scan' (T tar,4).
Replace leaf array #4 with #5; collect 'Target Scan' (T tar,5).
Replace leaf array #5 with #6; collect 'Target Scan' (T tar,6).
